item.content:encoded:
The global movement to recognize and protect the Rights of Nature continues to gain momentum, and forNature is seeking an experienced professional to play a central role in one of its most ambitious international initiatives. The organization is currently recruiting a full-time Initiative Coordinator based in Panama City, Panama, to support the operational, strategic, institutional, and diplomatic coordination of the initiative advancing the adoption of a United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature (UDRoN). This is a unique opportunity for professionals with experience in project coordination, international relations, environmental governance, multilateral diplomacy, and institutional engagement to contribute directly to an initiative with global environmental significance.

The successful candidate will coordinate complex international workstreams involving governments, legal experts, communications professionals, civil society organizations, diplomatic missions, and international institutions while working closely with the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Panama (MiAmbiente).

About the Initiative

The United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature (UDRoN) initiative seeks to advance international recognition of Nature as a subject of rights through the United Nations system.

The Initiative Coordinator will play a critical role in ensuring that all aspects of the initiative progress efficiently by coordinating institutional relationships, facilitating communication among stakeholders, tracking deliverables, and supporting diplomatic and legal processes.

The position sits at the intersection of environmental policy, international diplomacy, legal coordination, strategic communications, and institutional management.

Position Overview

The Initiative Coordinator will serve as the central coordination hub for the initiative.

Working closely with forNature and MiAmbiente, the coordinator will oversee operational implementation while ensuring that all teams remain aligned with project priorities, timelines, and strategic objectives. The role combines project management, stakeholder coordination, diplomatic engagement, documentation, communications management, and international event coordination.Although the position is remote, the successful applicant must be based in Panama City and remain available for meetings with Panamanian institutions, as well as occasional international travel.

Major Responsibilities

The Initiative Coordinator will oversee numerous interconnected workstreams.

1. Coordinate the Entire Initiative Team

The successful candidate will coordinate professionals across multiple disciplines, including:

  • Attorneys
  • Legal advisors
  • Communications specialists
  • Public Relations teams
  • Campaign consultants
  • Digital communications consultants
  • Graphic designers
  • Civil society engagement leads
  • Business engagement leads
  • Institutional advisors

Responsibilities include:

  • Acting as the central coordination point
  • Organizing internal workflows
  • Monitoring deadlines
  • Tracking assignments
  • Coordinating deliverables
  • Ensuring smooth communication across all teams
  • Monitoring approvals
  • Supporting strategic decision-making
  • Facilitating collaboration across departments

2. Lead Cross-Functional Team Coordination

The coordinator will organize and facilitate:

  • Internal meetings
  • Strategic planning sessions
  • Briefings
  • Coordination meetings
  • Follow-up discussions

They will also prepare:

  • Agendas
  • Meeting summaries
  • Action items
  • Briefing notes
  • Follow-up communications

The role requires maintaining alignment across legal, diplomatic, operational, communications, campaign, and institutional workstreams.

3. Serve as the Main Institutional Liaison

One of the most important aspects of this position involves serving as the day-to-day operational liaison between forNature and the Government of Panama.

Responsibilities include:

  • Coordinating with MiAmbiente
  • Working with the Office of International Technical Cooperation
  • Supporting coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
  • Managing institutional documentation
  • Tracking ministerial approvals
  • Following document management procedures
  • Maintaining continuity during government personnel transitions
  • Escalating institutional bottlenecks when necessary

4. Support Multilateral Diplomacy

The Initiative Coordinator will provide operational support for international diplomatic engagement.

Responsibilities include:

  • Preparing briefing materials
  • Developing talking points
  • Coordinating bilateral meetings
  • Supporting Panama’s Permanent Missions
  • Assisting embassies
  • Preparing diplomatic correspondence
  • Monitoring United Nations calendars
  • Tracking General Assembly timelines
  • Monitoring multilateral environmental agreement processes

The coordinator will also maintain records of:

  • Member State engagement
  • Government focal points
  • Expressions of support
  • Pending diplomatic actions

5. Document Production and Knowledge Management

The coordinator will oversee document development and information management across the initiative.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Creating the initiative’s Operations Manual
  • Drafting institutional documents
  • Producing concept notes
  • Preparing FAQs
  • Writing meeting records
  • Maintaining terminology consistency
  • Managing bilingual documentation
  • Tracking document versions
  • Protecting confidential materials
  • Organizing centralized documentation systems

Documentation will be prepared in both English and Spanish.

6. Support the For Nature Coalition of States

The coordinator will help expand and manage the growing Coalition of States supporting the initiative.

Responsibilities include:

  • Maintaining communication with participating countries
  • Tracking engagement records
  • Supporting onboarding processes
  • Preparing participation documents
  • Coordinating announcements
  • Managing membership materials
  • Supporting signing ceremonies during international events

7. Build Relationships with Key Stakeholders

The Initiative Coordinator will engage a broad range of stakeholders including:

  • Government institutions
  • International organizations
  • United Nations agencies
  • Academic institutions
  • Research organizations
  • Development partners
  • Philanthropic organizations
  • Business associations
  • Private sector organizations
  • Professional organizations
  • Legal institutions
  • Cultural institutions
  • Subnational governments

The coordinator will also support engagement with:

  • Civil society organizations
  • Indigenous Peoples
  • Traditional authorities
  • Community leaders
  • Local communities

8. Coordinate International Events

Responsibilities include organizing the initiative’s participation in international meetings and conferences by managing:

  • Side event proposals
  • Concept notes
  • Accreditation
  • Speaker coordination
  • Logistics
  • Official programme registration

9. Promote an Intercultural and Politically Sensitive Approach

The coordinator must ensure that implementation reflects:

  • Respect for Indigenous worldviews
  • Cultural diversity
  • Territorial knowledge systems
  • Diplomatic sensitivities
  • Institutional priorities
  • Political contexts surrounding the Rights of Nature movement

Required Qualifications

Applicants should possess substantial professional experience in areas such as:

  • Project coordination
  • Programme management
  • Institutional coordination
  • Campaign implementation

Candidates should demonstrate the ability to:

  • Coordinate multiple projects simultaneously
  • Manage competing priorities
  • Meet strict deadlines
  • Work independently
  • Communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders
  • Handle confidential information professionally

Essential Skills

Successful applicants should have:

  • Professional fluency in English
  • Professional fluency in Spanish
  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Strong written communication skills
  • Strong verbal communication skills
  • Excellent stakeholder management abilities
  • Experience preparing reports and institutional documents
  • Experience managing calendars and workplans
  • Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams

Preferred Experience

Additional advantages include experience with:

  • Government institutions
  • International organizations
  • Civil society networks
  • Environmental initiatives
  • Multilateral diplomacy
  • United Nations processes
  • Environmental law
  • Rights of Nature frameworks
  • Diplomatic drafting
  • Institutional relationship management
  • Panamanian public administration

Additional Requirements

Applicants should also possess:

  • A valid passport
  • A valid United States visa
  • Availability for international travel
  • Ability to coordinate across multiple time zones
  • Strong intercultural awareness
  • Respect for Indigenous leadership and governance systems

Work Location

The position is based in:

Panama City, Panama

The work arrangement is:

  • Full-time
  • Remote
  • Attendance at meetings with Panamanian institutions when required
  • Participation in in-person national and international engagements as necessary

The engagement is structured as an independent contractor relationship rather than direct employment.

Compensation

forNature offers:

  • Competitive industry compensation
  • Salary based on qualifications
  • Salary based on years of relevant experience

Application Requirements

Interested applicants should submit:

  • A current CV or résumé
  • A brief cover letter written in either English or Spanish

Applications should be emailed  via (info@fornature.org) with the subject line: Application – Initiative Coordinator

Application Deadline

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

There is no fixed application deadline, and candidates with immediate availability are strongly preferred.

Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since recruitment may conclude once a suitable candidate has been identified.

Equal Opportunity Employer

forNature is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace.

The organization does not discriminate on the basis of:

  • Race
  • Color
  • Religion
  • Sex
  • Gender identity
  • Sexual orientation
  • National origin
  • Age
  • Disability
  • Any other legally protected status

The organization strongly encourages applications from:

  • Women
  • Indigenous professionals
  • Individuals from historically marginalized communities.

learn more about the opportunity HERE

Why You Should Apply

This position offers an exceptional opportunity to contribute to an internationally significant environmental initiative that seeks to shape the future of global environmental governance. Professionals interested in diplomacy, international law, environmental protection, public policy, institutional coordination, and multilateral cooperation will find this role particularly rewarding.

Beyond project coordination, the successful candidate will help facilitate collaboration between governments, international organizations, civil society, and legal experts while supporting one of the most ambitious international efforts to advance the Rights of Nature within the United Nations framework.

The position provides meaningful exposure to global environmental diplomacy, strategic communications, institutional development, and international stakeholder engagement, making it an excellent opportunity for experienced professionals looking to make a lasting impact on international environmental policy.

Conclusion

The Initiative Coordinator position at forNature represents an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals passionate about environmental governance, international cooperation, and sustainable development. Working closely with Panama’s Ministry of Environment and a broad network of international stakeholders, the successful candidate will coordinate high-level legal, diplomatic, operational, and communications activities supporting the advancement of the United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature.With competitive compensation, international exposure, meaningful responsibilities, and the chance to contribute to a transformative global environmental initiative, this role is ideal for professionals who thrive in fast-paced, multicultural environments and are committed to advancing environmental justice and global cooperation.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026, an exciting international opportunity designed for young people who are passionate about environmental conservation, geography, mapping, and data-driven storytelling.

This fully remote, part-time externship provides participants with the opportunity to work alongside experts from two of the world’s leading conservation organizations the National Geographic Society and The Nature Conservancy while developing practical skills in Geographic Information Systems (GIS), community conservation, data visualization, environmental research, and science communication.

Running for eight weeks, the externship offers a flexible schedule requiring approximately 10 hours per week, making it suitable for students and young professionals who want to gain valuable international experience while balancing their studies or other commitments.

Participants who successfully complete the program will also receive a $500 educational stipend to help offset internet and technology costs associated with participation.

About the National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation Externship

Environmental challenges such as biodiversity loss, climate change, freshwater scarcity, and marine ecosystem degradation continue to affect communities across the globe. Solving these challenges requires innovative thinkers who can use science, technology, data, and storytelling to create meaningful change.

The National Geographic Society and The Nature Conservancy have partnered to launch this unique externship to equip young people with practical conservation skills while empowering them to address environmental challenges within their own communities.

Participants will learn how geographic information and mapping technologies can be used to understand conservation issues, communicate scientific findings, and influence local action.

Rather than focusing only on theory, the program combines learning with practical application, allowing participants to complete hands-on projects using real-world environmental data.

Externship Overview

The program offers an engaging learning experience with the following features:

  • Duration: 8 weeks
  • Start Date: 14 September 2026
  • Format: Fully remote
  • Commitment: Approximately 10 hours per week
  • Educational Stipend: $500 upon successful completion
  • Meetings: Recorded for flexible participation
  • Eligibility Age: 18–25 years
  • Geographic Eligibility: Open worldwide

Because the externship is conducted entirely online, participants from any country can take part without relocating.

What Participants Will Learn

Throughout the eight-week program, participants will explore major conservation issues while developing technical and professional skills that are highly valued across environmental and sustainability careers.

Major learning areas include:

1. Biodiversity and Community Conservation

Participants will study some of today’s most pressing environmental issues, including:

  • Biodiversity loss
  • Conservation solutions
  • Marine ecosystem protection
  • Freshwater conservation
  • Community-based conservation initiatives

They will also examine the relationship between geography, ecosystems, and local communities.

2. Geographic Information Systems (GIS)

One of the major highlights of the externship is practical training in Geographic Information Systems (GIS).

Participants will gain foundational knowledge of GIS technologies used worldwide to:

  • Collect geographic information
  • Manage environmental datasets
  • Analyze spatial information
  • Create professional maps
  • Support conservation planning
  • Visualize environmental challenges

The program uses Esri GIS mapping tools, one of the world’s leading geographic information platforms.

3. Data Visualization

Participants will learn how to transform complex environmental information into visual stories that communicate conservation challenges effectively.

This includes:

  • Visual mapping
  • Spatial data presentation
  • Interactive storytelling
  • Geographic data interpretation

4. Community Research

Participants will conduct research focused on conservation issues affecting their own local communities.

This includes:

  • Identifying environmental challenges
  • Collecting location-based information
  • Researching local biodiversity concerns
  • Investigating community conservation efforts

5. Public Speaking and Science Communication

Strong communication is essential for conservation leadership.

Participants will build confidence by learning how to:

  • Present research findings
  • Explain complex scientific concepts
  • Deliver engaging presentations
  • Communicate conservation solutions effectively

6. Conservation Storytelling

Using Esri StoryMaps, participants will create engaging digital stories that combine:

  • Maps
  • Images
  • Research
  • Geographic information
  • Environmental narratives

These projects become valuable portfolio pieces for future academic and professional opportunities.

Projects Participants Will Complete

Throughout the externship, participants will work on practical assignments, including:

  • Researching conservation issues in their communities
  • Creating maps using GIS software
  • Visualizing environmental data
  • Developing interactive Esri StoryMaps
  • Presenting conservation solutions
  • Collaborating with conservation experts

Skills Participants Will Gain

By the end of the externship, participants will have developed a broad range of transferable skills, including:

Conservation Literacy

Participants will gain a deeper understanding of:

  • Biodiversity conservation
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Geographic conservation strategies
  • Community resilience

Research Skills

Participants will practice:

  • Primary research
  • Secondary research
  • Data collection
  • Information analysis
  • Insight development

Community-Based Problem Solving

Participants will learn structured approaches for:

  • Identifying conservation gaps
  • Designing realistic environmental solutions
  • Addressing local conservation challenges

Cross-Sector Collaboration

Participants will work with professionals from:

  • National Geographic Society
  • The Nature Conservancy

They will gain valuable exposure to collaborative conservation work involving scientists, communicators, and community organizations.

Portfolio Development

Every participant will produce a professional Esri StoryMap that demonstrates their:

  • Research ability
  • Mapping skills
  • Data visualization expertise
  • Conservation storytelling

This project can strengthen future applications for scholarships, fellowships, internships, employment, and grants.

Systems Thinking

Participants will explore how global environmental challenges affect local ecosystems and communities while developing solutions that connect local action with broader conservation goals.

What Participants Receive

Successful participants will benefit from numerous professional development opportunities, including:

  • Hands-on conservation experience
  • Direct mentorship from National Geographic Society experts
  • Guidance from The Nature Conservancy professionals
  • GIS and mapping training
  • Environmental research experience
  • Science communication skills
  • Public speaking experience
  • Portfolio-ready conservation project
  • International networking opportunities
  • Flexible online participation
  • $500 educational stipend upon successful completion

About the National Geographic Society

Founded in 1888, the National Geographic Society is a global nonprofit organization committed to advancing science, exploration, education, and storytelling.

The organization has:

  • Awarded more than 15,000 grants worldwide
  • Supported research across all seven continents
  • Reached millions of students through educational initiatives
  • Inspired global audiences through science and exploration

About The Nature Conservancy

The Nature Conservancy is one of the world’s leading environmental nonprofit organizations.

Its mission focuses on protecting the lands and waters upon which all life depends while addressing:

  • Climate change
  • Biodiversity conservation
  • Sustainable ecosystems
  • Community resilience

The organization works globally to create a future where both people and nature thrive.

Why You Should Apply

This externship is ideal for young people interested in:

  • Environmental conservation
  • Climate action
  • Geography
  • GIS mapping
  • Sustainability
  • Environmental communication
  • Research
  • Science storytelling
  • Data visualization
  • Community engagement

APPLY HERE

No previous experience in GIS, conservation, or environmental science is required.

Participants only need curiosity, enthusiasm, and a willingness to learn.

Who Should Apply?

The externship is especially suitable for individuals who:

  • Are between 18 and 25 years old
  • Care about environmental issues
  • Want to understand how conservation affects communities
  • Are interested in GIS and mapping technologies
  • Enjoy research and problem-solving
  • Want to build an international professional portfolio
  • Prefer flexible remote learning opportunities
  • Have not previously participated in a National Geographic Society + The Nature Conservancy Externship

Application Process

Interested applicants should submit their applications through the official application platform before the closing date.

Because applications are expected to be highly competitive, prospective participants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

Important Dates

  • Application Deadline: 30 August 2026
  • Externship Start Date: 14 September 2026
  • Duration: 8 weeks
  • Commitment: Approximately 10 hours per week
  • Mode: Fully remote

Visit HERE to learn more about the National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026

Conclusion

The National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026 offers an outstanding opportunity for young people worldwide to gain practical conservation experience while learning from internationally recognized environmental organizations. Through expert mentorship, GIS training, conservation research, and storytelling, participants will develop skills that are increasingly valuable in careers related to sustainability, environmental policy, conservation science, education, and community development.

Beyond the technical knowledge, participants will build a professional portfolio, expand their global network, and contribute meaningful conservation solutions within their own communities. With a fully remote format, flexible schedule, and a $500 educational stipend, this externship provides an accessible pathway for the next generation of conservation leaders to make a lasting impact.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.

item.content:encoded:
The National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) is inviting applications for its Collaborative Research Grants 2026, a prestigious funding opportunity designed to advance knowledge in the humanities through collaborative scholarship. The program supports teams of researchers working together on projects that produce significant interpretive outputs such as books, digital publications, scholarly websites, peer-reviewed journal issues, and other sustainable research resources.

With awards of up to $250,000, this funding opportunity provides scholars and institutions with the resources needed to pursue innovative humanities research that contributes to a deeper understanding of the history and culture of the United States and Western civilization.

About the NEH Collaborative Research Program

The Collaborative Research Program supports teams of scholars engaged in humanities research that addresses important research questions through collaborative approaches. Projects may be based within a single discipline or bring together expertise from multiple fields.

NEH encourages projects that:

* Advance humanities scholarship.
* Incorporate diverse perspectives and approaches.
* Explore new areas of inquiry.
* Foster interdisciplinary collaboration.
* Produce tangible and sustainable scholarly outputs.

Collaborators may come from a single institution or multiple institutions, and international partnerships are welcome provided that scholars at U.S. institutions make substantial contributions to the project.

Funding Categories

The 2026 competition supports three project categories:

1. Planning International Collaboration

Supports the development of international humanities research partnerships and collaborative projects.

Maximum Award:  Up to $50,000

2. Manuscript Preparation

Supports collaborative research leading to scholarly books, edited volumes, and peer-reviewed publications.

3. Scholarly Digital Project

Supports the creation of digital humanities resources, databases, websites, and digital publications that advance humanities scholarship.

Funding Benefits

Successful applicants may receive:

* Funding of up to $250,000 depending on project category.
* Support for collaborative humanities research.
* Resources for manuscript development and publication.
* Funding for digital humanities projects.
* Opportunities to establish international research partnerships.
* Support for interdisciplinary and cross-institutional collaboration.

Expected Project Outputs

Projects must result in a tangible and sustainable product, including:

* Co-authored books
* Edited scholarly volumes
* Themed issues of peer-reviewed journals
* Digital publications
* Scholarly websites
* Digital humanities resources

Outputs should demonstrate meaningful collaboration and contribute to significant humanities research questions.

Eligible Applicants

The program is open to organizations and institutions supporting humanities research teams.

Collaborators may come from:

* Universities and colleges
* Research institutions
* Cultural organizations
* Humanities centers
* Nonprofit organizations

International collaboration is encouraged, but U.S.-based scholars must play a significant role in the project.

2026 Program Priority

For the 2026 funding cycle, proposed projects must focus on:

* The history of the United States
* The culture of the United States
* Western civilization

Applicants should ensure that their projects align clearly with these thematic priorities.

Project Duration

Depending on the funding category, projects may receive support for up to:

Three Years

This allows research teams sufficient time to complete substantial humanities projects and produce high-quality scholarly outputs.

Application Timeline

| Application Opens | July 7, 2026 |
| Application Deadline | September 16, 2026 |

Applicants are encouraged to begin preparations early to allow sufficient time for institutional approvals and registration requirements.

Application Process

 Step 1: Review the Funding Opportunity

Carefully read the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and related application guidance documents.

Step 2: Complete Required Registrations

Applicants must have active registrations with:

* SAM.gov
* Grants.gov

Organizations should verify that their registrations are current before beginning the application process.

Step 3: Prepare the Application

Develop a strong proposal that clearly outlines:

* Research objectives
* Collaborative structure
* Project methodology
* Expected outcomes
* Dissemination plans

Step 4: Submit Through Grants.gov

Applications must be submitted electronically through Grants.gov before the deadline.

Why Apply?

The NEH Collaborative Research Grants represent one of the leading funding opportunities for humanities scholars seeking to undertake ambitious collaborative research projects. Whether developing a major scholarly publication, creating innovative digital resources, or building international partnerships, this program provides the financial support needed to generate lasting contributions to humanities scholarship.

The program also encourages interdisciplinary collaboration and supports projects that bring together diverse expertise to address complex research questions in new and meaningful ways.

Contact Information

Division of Research
National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH)

📧 [collaborative@neh.gov](mailto:collaborative@neh.gov)
📞 202-606-8200

Conclusion

The NEH Collaborative Research Grants 2026 offer a remarkable opportunity for humanities researchers and institutions to collaborate on projects that expand knowledge, generate impactful scholarship, and contribute to a deeper understanding of the United States and Western civilization. With funding of up to $250,000, support for international collaboration, and opportunities to create lasting scholarly resources, this program is ideal for teams seeking to advance innovative humanities research. Interested applicants should begin preparing their proposals now and submit their applications before the September 16, 2026 deadline.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), through the United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme, is inviting qualified professionals to apply for the Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia) National UN Volunteer assignment based in Suva, Fiji. This is an excellent opportunity for experienced communications professionals with strong digital media, storytelling, multimedia production, and social media management skills to contribute to improving the lives of children and young people across the Pacific region.

The assignment offers professionals an opportunity to work directly with UNICEF’s Communication Section, supporting advocacy campaigns, multimedia storytelling, digital communications, donor visibility initiatives, and audience engagement across 14 Pacific Island countries.

If you have experience in digital communications, content creation, photography, videography, multimedia editing, analytics, and strategic communication, this assignment provides a meaningful platform to apply your expertise while supporting one of the world’s leading humanitarian organizations.

About UNICEF

UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to protect the rights and wellbeing of every child. Its mission is to ensure that every child survives, thrives, learns, and is protected from violence, discrimination, and exploitation.

Within the Pacific region, UNICEF serves:

  • Cook Islands
  • Fiji
  • Kiribati
  • Marshall Islands
  • Federated States of Micronesia
  • Nauru
  • Niue
  • Palau
  • Samoa
  • Solomon Islands
  • Tokelau
  • Tonga
  • Tuvalu
  • Vanuatu

Together, these countries are home to approximately 2.3 million people, including 1.2 million children and youth, living across more than 660 islands and atolls spread over approximately 17.2 million square kilometres of the Pacific Ocean.

Several countries within the region—including Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tuvalu—are classified as Fragile States under World Bank/OECD criteria, making UNICEF’s work particularly significant.

About the Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia) Assignment

The Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia) will be part of UNICEF Pacific’s Communications Section and will report directly to the Digital Communication Officer.

The Communications Section supports all UNICEF programme areas through strategic communication, advocacy, media engagement, branding, digital outreach, and social media campaigns.

The team also leads advocacy around four major regional priorities:

  • Violence against children
  • Climate action
  • Water security
  • Nutrition

The selected volunteer will help strengthen UNICEF’s digital presence, produce engaging multimedia content, enhance donor visibility, support youth participation, and amplify UNICEF’s advocacy messages through innovative storytelling.

Assignment Information

Item Details
Host Organization UNICEF
Volunteer Programme United Nations Volunteers (UNV)
Position Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia)
Duty Station Suva, Fiji
Assignment Type National UN Volunteer
Volunteer Category Specialist
Work Arrangement Full-time
Work Location On UN Premises
Duration 12 Months
Extension Possibility Yes
Expected Start Date 24 August 2026
Number of Vacancies 1

Main Responsibilities

The Communications Officer will undertake a wide range of responsibilities covering digital communications, multimedia production, analytics, storytelling, advocacy, and volunteer engagement.

1. Digital Communication Planning and Publishing

The successful candidate will support UNICEF’s online communication strategy by:

  • Planning digital communication activities.
  • Producing digital communication materials.
  • Publishing content across UNICEF’s website and digital platforms.
  • Supporting social media campaigns.
  • Coordinating promotional campaigns.
  • Developing communication materials aligned with regional and global priorities.
  • Supporting donor visibility planning.
  • Coordinating production timelines.
  • Monitoring donor branding requirements.
  • Maintaining influencer and advocacy databases.
  • Supporting youth engagement initiatives.
  • Assisting online participation campaigns.

2. Multimedia Storytelling

A major component of the role involves creating compelling multimedia stories that demonstrate UNICEF’s impact.

Responsibilities include:

  • Producing social media reels.
  • Editing short videos.
  • Creating photo stories.
  • Designing graphics.
  • Preparing presentation assets.
  • Using existing photo and video libraries.
  • Capturing photographs during events.
  • Recording field missions.
  • Covering programme visits.
  • Documenting humanitarian activities.
  • Working with programme teams to identify impactful stories.
  • Simplifying complex development programmes into engaging public stories.
  • Coordinating interviews.
  • Supporting scripting.
  • Managing filming schedules.
  • Editing content.
  • Incorporating feedback.
  • Preparing final products for publication.

3. Ensuring UNICEF Brand Standards

The officer will ensure all communication materials comply with UNICEF standards by following:

  • UNICEF branding guidelines.
  • Ethical storytelling practices.
  • Child safeguarding policies.
  • Image consent procedures.
  • Accessibility standards.
  • Inclusion principles.

4. Digital Analytics and Performance Monitoring

The role also requires continuous monitoring of digital performance.

Responsibilities include:

  • Tracking engagement rates.
  • Monitoring audience growth.
  • Measuring reach.
  • Assessing impressions.
  • Reviewing click-through rates.
  • Preparing campaign performance reports.
  • Identifying successful content trends.
  • Testing new communication approaches.
  • Monitoring audience feedback.

5. Supporting the UN Volunteers Programme

  • Celebrate International Volunteer Day.
  • Produce annual volunteer reports.
  • Share field stories for UNV publications.
  • Mentor newly arrived volunteers through the Buddy Programme.

Required Skills and Experience

Applicants should possess at least three years of professional experience in communications or related fields.

Essential competencies include:

  • Professional digital communications experience.
  • Social media management.
  • Multimedia editing.
  • Photography.
  • Videography.
  • Storytelling.
  • Graphic content production.
  • Copywriting.
  • Editing.
  • Proofreading.
  • Project management.
  • Organizational skills.
  • Communication planning.
  • Digital monitoring.
  • Analytics.
  • Teamwork.
  • Remote collaboration.
  • Strong interpersonal communication.

Candidates should also demonstrate commitment to UNICEF’s CRITAS values:

  • Care
  • Respect
  • Integrity
  • Trust
  • Accountability
  • Sustainability

Desirable Skills

  • Digital analytics experience.

  • Adobe Photoshop.
  • Adobe Lightroom.
  • Adobe Illustrator.
  • Adobe InDesign.
  • Content Management Systems (CMS).
  • NGO experience.
  • UN experience.
  • Spreadsheet management.
  • Database management.
  • Technical writing.
  • Translating technical documents into public-friendly messages.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must possess:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in:
    • Communications
    • Journalism
    • Or another closely related discipline

Language Requirements

Applicants must demonstrate:

  • Fluent English (required)

Core Competencies

UNICEF seeks professionals who demonstrate:

  • Accountability
  • Adaptability
  • Flexibility
  • Building Trust
  • Commitment
  • Motivation
  • Continuous Learning
  • Communication
  • Creativity
  • Ethics
  • Integrity
  • Planning
  • Organizing
  • Professionalism
  • Respect for Diversity
  • Self-management
  • Technological Awareness
  • Teamwork

Areas of Expertise

Successful candidates should have experience in one or more of the following:

  • Communications
  • Public Information
  • Advocacy
  • Writing
  • Editing
  • Proofreading
  • Research
  • Reporting
  • Knowledge Management

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must:

  • Be between 18 and 80 years of age.
  • Be a national of Fiji, a legal resident of Fiji, or hold refugee status in Fiji.
  • Have at least three years of relevant professional experience.
  • Meet the required educational qualifications.
  • Demonstrate fluency in English.

Living and Working in Fiji

The assignment is based in Suva, the capital city of Fiji.

UNICEF notes that:

  • Fiji is considered a middle-income country.
  • Basic services are readily available.
  • The country is widely recognized for its welcoming and friendly communities.
  • Volunteers are expected to arrange their own accommodation and living arrangements.
  • Standard personal security precautions should be observed.

Inclusivity and Equal Opportunity

UNICEF and the United Nations Volunteers programme strongly encourage diversity and inclusion.

Applications are welcomed regardless of:

  • Gender
  • Race
  • Religion
  • Nationality
  • Ethnicity
  • Disability
  • Sexual orientation
  • Gender identity
  • Language
  • Social origin
  • Pregnancy
  • Age

Reasonable accommodation is available for volunteers with disabilities throughout recruitment and during the assignment.

COVID-19 Requirement

Selected volunteers must generally provide proof of full COVID-19 vaccination with a World Health Organization (WHO)-endorsed vaccine before assuming duty, where applicable under UNICEF policies. Certain remote assignments or assignments without community interaction may be exempt according to UNICEF guidelines.

Scam Warning

Applicants should remember that:

  • The United Nations never charges application fees.
  • No payment is required at any stage of recruitment.
  • Applicants should be cautious of fraudulent recruitment schemes and only apply through official UN platforms.

Why You Should Apply

This assignment offers communications professionals an exceptional opportunity to:

  • Build experience within UNICEF.
  • Strengthen digital communication and multimedia production skills.
  • Work on high-impact advocacy campaigns.
  • Produce stories that improve children’s lives.
  • Gain exposure to international development communication.

  • Develop expertise in donor visibility and digital analytics.
  • Contribute directly to UNICEF’s mission of protecting children’s rights.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

No application deadline has been specified in the vacancy information. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as recruitment may close once a suitable number of applications has been received.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia) at UNICEF Fiji.

Conclusion

The UNICEF Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia) National UN Volunteer assignment presents an outstanding opportunity for experienced communications professionals in Fiji who are passionate about digital storytelling, multimedia production, and advocacy. Working within UNICEF’s Pacific Office, the selected volunteer will play a central role in creating compelling digital content that highlights the organization’s impact across 14 Pacific Island countries while strengthening public awareness of children’s rights and development priorities.

Beyond professional growth, this assignment provides the chance to contribute to meaningful humanitarian work, collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, and support campaigns that influence policy, engage young people, and improve the lives of children throughout the Pacific region. item.content:encoded:
The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust (OMT) has officially opened applications for its prestigious Postgraduate Scholarships for students planning to begin their studies between January and June 2027. The Trust continues its long-standing commitment to developing exceptional academic talent by supporting outstanding scholars pursuing Master’s, Doctoral, and Postdoctoral studies in South Africa and, in exceptional cases, internationally.

The scholarship is designed for individuals with an exceptional academic record who aspire to make significant contributions to academia, scientific research, innovation, development, public policy, and other fields that advance knowledge and benefit society. Every year, the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust awards a limited number of highly competitive scholarships to scholars who demonstrate excellence, leadership potential, and a commitment to using their advanced education to contribute meaningfully to South Africa’s future.

Applications for students intending to commence studies between January and June 2027 are currently open and will close on 31 August 2026.

About the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust

The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust is one of South Africa’s leading philanthropic organizations dedicated to supporting higher education, research, youth development, and initiatives that strengthen the country’s knowledge economy.

Through its postgraduate scholarship programme, the Trust invests in future academics, researchers, innovators, and professionals whose work has the potential to address national and global challenges. The scholarship programme has supported numerous distinguished researchers and scholars whose work has gained international recognition across multiple disciplines.

The Trust believes that investing in highly talented individuals contributes directly to strengthening South Africa’s research capacity, universities, innovation ecosystem, and long-term development.

OMT Postgraduate Scholarship Programme 2027

The scholarship programme supports postgraduate studies at three academic levels:

  • Master’s Degree
  • Doctoral (PhD) Degree
  • Postdoctoral Research

Each year, only a limited number of scholarships are awarded, making the programme highly competitive. Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate exceptional academic achievement together with clear plans for using their education to contribute to research, teaching, development, or other knowledge-driven sectors.

International Study Opportunities

The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust also provides funding for international postgraduate study, although this opportunity is reserved only for exceptional candidates.

Applicants seeking international scholarships must demonstrate one or more of the following:

  • Their proposed programme is in a unique or highly specialized discipline that is not readily available in South Africa.
  • The intended international institution offers expertise unavailable locally.
  • Study under internationally recognized experts or global leaders will significantly advance their field.
  • International training will contribute meaningfully to their future academic or research career and ultimately benefit South Africa.

International scholarships are therefore considered only in exceptional circumstances and require strong academic justification.

Fields of Study

Applications are welcomed from all academic disciplines, ensuring that scholars from diverse areas of study have an opportunity to compete for funding.

However, the Trust specifically excludes:

  • Master of Business Administration (MBA) programmes
  • Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) programmes
  • Programmes with a narrow commercial focus

Apart from these exclusions, applicants across sciences, engineering, humanities, social sciences, medicine, agriculture, environmental sciences, education, arts, technology, law, and many other disciplines are encouraged to apply.

Who Should Apply?

The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust seeks applicants who demonstrate exceptional academic ability together with a strong vision for their future contribution to society.

Ideal candidates include individuals who:

  • Have consistently demonstrated academic excellence.
  • Intend to pursue careers in:
    • Academia
    • Research
    • Innovation
    • Development
    • Public policy
    • Related knowledge-intensive sectors.
  • Have well-developed postgraduate research plans.
  • Show the potential to become leaders in their disciplines.
  • Intend to use their expertise to strengthen research and development within South Africa.

Preference for Local Universities

Although international study is supported in exceptional cases, the Trust indicates that preference may be given to students pursuing postgraduate studies at South African universities.

This reflects the Trust’s commitment to strengthening local higher education institutions while still supporting international opportunities where clearly justified.

Scholarship Features

Successful scholars benefit from:

  • Funding for Master’s studies.
  • Funding for Doctoral (PhD) studies.
  • Funding for Postdoctoral research.
  • Possible international scholarship support for exceptional candidates.
  • Recognition through one of South Africa’s most prestigious postgraduate scholarship programmes.
  • Opportunities to advance academic and research careers.
  • Support for research that contributes to South Africa’s development.
  • Access to a respected network of scholars and researchers.

Selection Process

The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust follows a highly competitive selection process.

Applications are assessed based on:

  • Academic excellence.
  • Quality of the proposed study or research.
  • Potential contribution to academia and research.
  • Career aspirations.
  • Relevance and impact of the proposed programme.
  • Availability of specialized training where international study is requested.

Awards are made entirely at the discretion of the Trust’s Trustees.

Important Application Guidelines

Applicants should carefully observe all application requirements before submitting their applications.

Key guidelines include:

  • Applications must be submitted through the official online application portal.
  • Incomplete applications will not be considered.
  • Applications sent by email will not be accepted.
  • Only complete online submissions submitted before the deadline will be reviewed.
  • Scholarship awards are made solely at the discretion of the Trustees.

Failure to comply with these requirements may result in disqualification.

Application Timeline

For studies commencing January to June 2027

  • Applications Open: 1 June 2026
  • Application Deadline: 31 August 2026

For studies commencing July to December 2026

  • Applications Open: 6 January 2026
  • Application Deadline: 31 March 2026

Applicants targeting the January–June 2027 intake should ensure they submit all required documents before the 31 August 2026 deadline.

APPLY HERE

Additional Opportunities Offered by the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust

Beyond postgraduate scholarships, the Trust also offers several prestigious programmes, including:

  • Harry Oppenheimer Fellowship
  • New Frontiers Research Award
  • Sabbatical Study opportunities

These initiatives continue to support leading academics and researchers making significant contributions within South Africa and internationally.

Why You Should Apply

The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarship is among South Africa’s most respected postgraduate funding opportunities. Beyond financial support, it recognizes academic excellence and empowers scholars to pursue impactful research that addresses societal challenges.

Whether your ambition is to become a university lecturer, researcher, scientist, innovator, or policy expert, this scholarship provides an opportunity to access world-class postgraduate education while contributing to South Africa’s academic and research landscape.

If you possess an outstanding academic record, a well-defined research vision, and a commitment to advancing knowledge for public benefit, this scholarship represents an excellent opportunity to further your academic journey.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to prepare all required documents early and submit complete applications through the official online portal before the closing date.

Visit HERE for more information about the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarships 2027 in South Africa.

Conclusion

The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarships 2027 offer exceptional funding opportunities for talented scholars pursuing Master’s, Doctoral, and Postdoctoral studies. With support available across nearly all academic disciplines and limited international scholarships for outstanding candidates, the programme aims to cultivate the next generation of researchers, academics, and innovators who will contribute to South Africa’s long-term development. Since the awards are highly competitive and only complete online applications are considered, interested candidates should begin preparing their applications well in advance and submit them before 31 August 2026 for the January–June 2027 intake.

For more global Scholarship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Higher education institutions seeking to strengthen international collaboration can now apply for the TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 under the Going Global Partnerships programme. The second round of funding offers 11 additional grants to support partnerships between institutions in the United Kingdom, Armenia, Bangladesh, and Thailand.

The grants aim to promote sustainable transnational education (TNE) partnerships that expand access to quality education, strengthen institutional collaboration, and contribute to positive change in local education systems.

About the TNE Exploratory Grants

The TNE Exploratory Grants support innovative projects that explore opportunities for transnational education partnerships while promoting inclusive and accessible international education.

The programme seeks to encourage institutions to better understand local educational contexts, develop sustainable partnerships, and contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through international education collaboration.

Grant Objectives

Projects should address one or more of the following objectives:

* Promote long-term and sustainable institutional change through Transnational Education (TNE).
* Increase access to high-quality and inclusive education.
* Improve understanding of local contexts and regulatory environments that support TNE partnerships.
* Strengthen operational frameworks for international education collaboration.
* Support education initiatives that respond to local needs and priorities.
* Contribute to positive changes in education systems and SDG achievement.

Funding Details

Grant Amount: Up to £25,000
*Project Duration: 17 months
*Project Start Date:  January 2027
* Number of Projects Funded: 11
* Programme: Going Global Partnerships
Participating Countries:  Armenia, Bangladesh, Thailand, and the United Kingdom

Eligibility Criteria

For Armenia and Bangladesh Partnerships

* The lead institution must be a UK higher education provider with degree-awarding powers.
* Partnerships should involve eligible institutions in Armenia or Bangladesh.

 For Thailand Partnerships

* The lead institution must be a Thai higher education institution.
* Partnerships should involve eligible UK institutions and meet programme requirements.

Applicants should consult the official Call Guidance document for complete eligibility requirements.

 Benefits of the Grant

Selected institutions will receive:

* Funding of up to £25,000.
* Opportunities to establish or strengthen international partnerships.
* Support for exploring sustainable TNE models.
* Enhanced institutional capacity for international collaboration.
* Opportunities to contribute to educational development and SDG-related outcomes.
* Greater understanding of local educational systems and regulatory frameworks.

Application Process

Applications must be submitted through the Going Global Partnerships online grant platform.

Armenia and Bangladesh Partnerships

Applicants should use:

Going Global Partnerships – Armenia & Bangladesh – TNE Exploratory Grants 2026

Applications can only be initiated and submitted by the lead UK institution.

Thailand Partnerships

Applicants should use:

Going Global Partnerships – Thailand – TNE Exploratory Grants 2026

Applications can only be initiated and submitted by the lead Thai institution.

Important Dates

Clarification Questions Deadline: 23 July 2026
Application Deadline: 2 September 2026, 11:59 a.m. BST
Project Start Date: January 2027

Why Apply?

The TNE Exploratory Grants provide an excellent opportunity for universities and higher education institutions to explore innovative international education partnerships. Beyond financial support, the programme helps institutions build long-term collaboration frameworks that improve educational access, quality, and sustainability across multiple countries.

Institutions interested in expanding their global engagement strategies and contributing to stronger international education systems should consider applying for this competitive funding opportunity.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the Going Global Partnerships online grant platform before the deadline.

Application Deadline:  2 September 2026

Conclusion

The TNE Exploratory Grants: Round 2 offer an excellent opportunity for higher education institutions in the UK, Armenia, Bangladesh, and Thailand to build innovative international partnerships that can transform access to quality education. With funding of up to £25,000 per project, successful applicants will have the chance to explore new transnational education models, strengthen institutional collaboration, and contribute to more inclusive and sustainable higher education systems.

Beyond financial support, these grants provide a platform for institutions to deepen international engagement, improve understanding of local educational contexts, and develop initiatives that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The programme encourages institutions to create long-term impact by fostering knowledge exchange, enhancing educational opportunities, and supporting positive policy and system-level changes.

If your institution is looking to establish or expand meaningful transnational education partnerships, this grant programme could be the catalyst needed to turn innovative ideas into impactful projects. Interested applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements and application guidance before submitting their proposals ahead of the 2 September 2026 deadline.

Discover more opportunities like these on the OFY webpage.

item.content:encoded:
Women around the world continue to drive innovation, lead communities, create groundbreaking solutions, and transform lives despite facing financial, structural, and social barriers. To help remove these obstacles and empower women to achieve even greater impact, applications are opening in August 2026 for a series of women-focused grant programs designed to provide financial support, mentorship, networking opportunities, and access to an inspiring community of changemakers.

These funding opportunities recognize women at different stages of their journeys. Whether you are already leading impactful initiatives, developing an innovative project that benefits women and girls, or seeking financial assistance to continue your education or overcome personal hardship, these programs are designed to provide meaningful support.

Rather than offering funding alone, the initiative combines financial backing with mentorship, leadership development, peer learning, and access to a valuable professional network, creating opportunities for long-term personal and professional growth.

Why These Women’s Grant Programs Matter

Women continue to face challenges in accessing funding, educational opportunities, leadership positions, and resources necessary to maximize their impact.

These grant programs seek to:

  • Remove financial barriers.
  • Recognize exceptional women leaders.
  • Support innovative ideas that benefit women and girls.
  • Invest in future female changemakers.
  • Build stronger communities through women’s leadership.
  • Create lasting public impact through funded initiatives.
  • Connect women with mentors and experienced professionals.
  • Foster collaboration through cohort experiences.

The programs acknowledge that women contribute to positive change across every profession, industry, and community.

Three Funding Opportunities Available

Applicants may apply under the category that best reflects their current stage, achievements, and goals.

1. Change Agent Prize

The Change Agent Prize recognizes accomplished women who have already demonstrated outstanding leadership and measurable impact in improving the lives of other women.

Rather than funding a future idea, this prize celebrates women who have an established record of creating meaningful change.

Eligible women may come from any professional background, including:

  • Education
  • Healthcare
  • Business
  • Technology
  • Science
  • Government
  • Community development
  • Arts and culture
  • Journalism
  • Social entrepreneurship
  • Human rights
  • Environmental conservation
  • Any other field where women are creating positive impact

Funding Available

Successful recipients may receive:

  • Up to $90,000 in funding.

Additional Benefits

Recipients may also access:

  • Mentorship opportunities (optional)
  • Cohort learning experience (optional)
  • Professional networking opportunities (optional)
  • Community of accomplished women leaders

This category is ideal for women who already have a proven history of breaking barriers and empowering other women.

2. Disruptor Award

The Disruptor Award supports women with innovative projects or ideas capable of creating substantial public benefit for women and girls.

Applicants do not necessarily need years of established impact but should present a credible, transformative concept with strong potential to improve lives.

Projects may focus on areas such as:

  • Women’s economic empowerment
  • Education
  • Health
  • Technology
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Leadership development
  • Gender equality
  • Climate resilience
  • Legal rights
  • Safety and protection
  • Financial inclusion
  • Social innovation
  • Community development

The project should clearly demonstrate how it will benefit women and girls on a broader scale.

Funding Available

Successful applicants may receive:

  • Up to $90,000.

Required Program Components

Recipients are expected to participate in:

  • Mentorship
  • Cohort experience

Network access is also available to participants.

The combination of funding and structured mentorship helps ensure projects have the greatest possible public impact.

3. Financial Aid Program

The Financial Aid Program supports women experiencing financial hardship who need assistance to take the next step toward achieving their goals.

The funding is intended for women who possess a clear vision for creating positive impact but currently lack the financial resources necessary to move forward.

Support may help women:

  • Continue their education
  • Pursue professional development
  • Overcome financial hardship
  • Invest in opportunities that increase future impact
  • Remove barriers preventing personal and professional growth

Funding Available

Recipients may receive:

  • Up to $30,000.

Additional Opportunities

Participants may also access:

  • Optional mentorship
  • Optional cohort experience
  • Optional networking opportunities

This program recognizes that financial barriers should not prevent talented women from realizing their potential.

Beyond Funding: Additional Benefits

Unlike many traditional grant opportunities, these programs provide much more than financial support.

Successful applicants may benefit from:

Mentorship

Participants gain access to experienced mentors who can provide:

  • Professional guidance
  • Leadership advice
  • Strategic planning support
  • Career development coaching

Cohort Experience

Participants join a community of women leaders, allowing them to:

  • Learn together
  • Share experiences
  • Collaborate on ideas
  • Build lifelong professional relationships

Network Access

Applicants may become part of an influential network that can open doors to:

  • Partnerships
  • Collaborations
  • Future funding opportunities
  • Career advancement
  • Leadership opportunities

Community Support

Recipients become part of a broader ecosystem committed to advancing women and expanding opportunities for future generations.

Who Should Apply?

These grant programs are designed for women at different stages of leadership and impact.

Ideal applicants include women who:

  • Have demonstrated leadership supporting women.
  • Are developing innovative ideas benefiting women and girls.
  • Need financial support to continue education.
  • Face financial barriers preventing future progress.
  • Want to scale their existing impact.
  • Are committed to improving the lives of other women.
  • Seek mentorship and professional growth.
  • Want to join a global network of changemakers.

Because applicants may come from any field or profession, the programs encourage diverse perspectives and experiences.

Funding Summary

Program Maximum Funding Mentorship Cohort Network Access
Change Agent Prize Up to $90,000 Optional Optional Optional
Disruptor Award Up to $90,000 Required Required Available
Financial Aid Up to $30,000 Optional Optional Optional

Application Timeline

  • Applications Open: August 2026
  • Application Deadline: Not yet announced

Applicants are encouraged to prepare their materials early and monitor official announcements for the closing date once it is released.

APPLY HERE

Why You Should Consider Applying

These programs provide a unique opportunity to access significant financial support while also benefiting from mentorship, peer learning, and professional networking.

Whether you are an established leader, an innovator with a transformative idea, or someone seeking financial assistance to unlock your potential, these grants are designed to remove barriers and help women achieve lasting impact.

By investing in women across different sectors and career stages, the initiative aims to create stronger communities, expand opportunities for women and girls, and accelerate meaningful social change.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Strong Women Grant Programs 2026.

Conclusion

The Women Grant Programs opening in August 2026 represent an important investment in women’s leadership, innovation, education, and social impact. With funding of up to $90,000 available under selected programs and additional benefits such as mentorship, cohort participation, and professional networking, the initiative goes beyond traditional grant funding to foster sustainable growth and long-term success.

Women who are creating change, developing impactful ideas, or overcoming financial obstacles should consider applying. Early preparation will strengthen applications, especially as the official deadline has not yet been announced.

For more grant opportunities visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming nearly every aspect of modern life, from education and healthcare to governance, business, communication, security, and public policy. As AI technologies continue to evolve, there is an increasing need for thoughtful discussions about how these innovations influence society, ethics, democracy, and human well-being.

To encourage informed public dialogue and nurture the next generation of thinkers in this important field, the AI Societal Impact Lab has officially launched applications for its inaugural Autumn 2026 Fellowship. This unique remote fellowship is designed to empower emerging voices interested in understanding and addressing the social, political, and ethical implications of artificial intelligence.

The fellowship provides participants with an opportunity to collaborate with like-minded individuals, receive expert mentorship, contribute original research, and become part of a growing international community focused on ensuring that AI development benefits society responsibly.

If you are a recent graduate, an early-career researcher, or someone passionate about the intersection of technology and society, this fellowship offers an outstanding platform to expand your knowledge, strengthen your analytical skills, and publish your ideas.

About the AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship

The Autumn 2026 Fellowship is an intensive online programme created to support individuals who want to critically examine how emerging artificial intelligence technologies are reshaping societies around the world.

Rather than focusing exclusively on the technical development of AI systems, the fellowship emphasizes broader societal questions, including governance, ethics, public policy, democracy, social justice, regulation, and the human consequences of technological advancement.

Participants will engage in collaborative discussions, workshops, research activities, and mentorship sessions designed to encourage interdisciplinary thinking and meaningful public engagement.

The programme aims to build a vibrant network of individuals committed to understanding and addressing the opportunities and challenges associated with rapidly advancing AI technologies.

Fellowship Duration

The fellowship will:

  • Run remotely for approximately 8–10 weeks
  • Begin in mid to late September 2026
  • Require approximately 4 hours of participation each week, including:
    • One hour of weekly group discussions or virtual calls
    • Three hours of independent study, research, or project work

The AI Societal Impact Lab will provide shortlisted candidates with the detailed programme schedule and specific dates.

Fellowship Curriculum

Participants can expect a structured programme combining collaborative learning with independent research.

The curriculum includes:

  • Weekly virtual fellowship meetings
  • Individual research and analytical work
  • Collaborative group projects
  • Expert-led workshops
  • Interactive seminars
  • Mentorship sessions
  • Preparation of a publishable analytical article

The fellowship is intentionally designed to encourage interdisciplinary collaboration among participants with diverse educational and professional backgrounds.

Fellowship Benefits

Selected fellows will enjoy numerous academic and professional development opportunities, including:

1. Become Part of an International Community

Participants will join a growing network of individuals committed to understanding and responding to the societal impacts of artificial intelligence.

2. Receive Expert Mentorship

Each fellow will receive mentorship from experienced fellows at the AI Societal Impact Lab, providing valuable guidance throughout the programme.

3. Collaborate on a Group Project

Participants will work together with fellow researchers and professionals on collaborative projects exploring real-world AI-related societal issues.

4. Publish an Original Analytical Article

Each fellow will produce an independent analytical piece that will be published on the AI Societal Impact Lab website, providing valuable publication experience and increasing professional visibility.

5. Participate in Workshops and Seminars

The fellowship includes specialized workshops and seminars focused on current debates surrounding artificial intelligence and society.

6. Develop Research and Analytical Skills

Participants will strengthen their abilities in:

  • Critical thinking
  • Policy analysis
  • Academic writing
  • Public communication
  • Collaborative research
  • Interdisciplinary problem-solving

7. Expand Professional Networks

The programme provides opportunities to connect with researchers, academics, policy experts, and fellow participants from diverse backgrounds.

Eligibility Criteria

item.content:encoded:
Introduction

The University of Bayreuth Centre of International Excellence “Alexander von Humboldt” (Bayreuth Humboldt Centre) has established itself as a hub for fostering international academic collaboration, advancing interdisciplinary research, and strengthening global scholarly networks. Through its Starter Grant Programme (2027) and Short Term Grant Programme (2026), the Centre provides researchers from around the world with opportunities to engage in innovative projects, collaborate with local hosts at Bayreuth, and contribute to the university’s vibrant research ecosystem.

These grants are not merely financial awards; they are instruments of academic exchange designed to break down barriers between disciplines, cultures, and generations of researchers. The Centre’s mission is to support projects of top academic quality, encourage diversity, and promote gender equality in research. By offering structured funding opportunities, the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre ensures that scholars can pursue ambitious projects while benefiting from the university’s infrastructure, networks, and intellectual environment.

The Starter Grant Programme provides €10,000 to support project costs, with an additional monthly family allowance for grantees accompanied by children. Successful completion of a Starter Grant opens the door to a Booster Grant (€20,000), contingent on documented outcomes such as joint publications, workshops, or conferences.

The Short Term Grant Programme supports research stays of 1–3 weeks, reimbursing travel and accommodation expenses up to €3,500. This programme is ideal for scholars seeking to establish collaborations, initiate joint projects, or explore new research directions in a condensed timeframe.

Both programmes require applicants to identify a local host at Bayreuth prior to submission, ensuring that projects are grounded in meaningful collaboration. The grants are open to all disciplines, with specific rulings for African Studies due to German Research Foundation regulations.

By participating in these programmes, researchers gain not only financial support but also access to Bayreuth’s world-class research networks, facilities, and intellectual community. The application deadline for both programmes is September 15, 2026.

Programme Details

1. Programme Overview

  • Starter Grant Programme (2027): €10,000 award, family allowance, eligibility for Booster Grant (€20,000).
  • Short Term Grant Programme (2026): Up to €3,500 reimbursement for travel and accommodation, 1–3 week stays.
  • Both programmes emphasise collaboration with a local host at Bayreuth.

2. Programme Goals

  • Promote academic exchange across disciplines and cultures.
  • Strengthen international networking with leading universities worldwide.
  • Encourage interdisciplinary research addressing societal challenges.
  • Support diversity and gender equality in research.

3. Candidate Requirements

  • Completed PhD (including diploma).
  • Affiliation with institutions abroad.
  • Projects must demonstrate academic excellence and potential for networking.
  • Applications must adhere to Application Guidelines.

4. Experience Bayreuth – Collaboration with Local Host

  • Applicants must identify a local host prior to submission.
  • Hosts provide office/lab space and infrastructure.
  • Projects must benefit both the candidate and the host.

5. Funding Details

  • Starter Grant: €10,000 + €250/month family allowance.
  • Booster Grant: €20,000 follow‑up funding upon successful completion.
  • Short Term Grant: Up to €3,500 reimbursement for travel/accommodation.

6. Application Process

  • Submit complete application via online form.
  • Required documents: personal statement, CV, project details.
  • Deadline: September 15, 2026.
  • Selection is merit‑based, focusing on academic excellence and project quality.

Apply HERE today!

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Q1: What is the purpose of the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre Grants? The grants aim to foster international collaboration, support interdisciplinary research, and strengthen Bayreuth’s global academic networks. They provide financial support and institutional affiliation to researchers pursuing innovative projects.

Q2: Who can apply for these grants? Academics, independent scholars, and professionals affiliated with institutions abroad who have completed their PhD are eligible. Applicants must propose projects of high academic quality and identify a local host at Bayreuth.

Q3: What is the difference between the Starter Grant and the Short Term Grant?

  • The Starter Grant (€10,000) supports longer-term projects and includes eligibility for a follow-up Booster Grant (€20,000).
  • The Short Term Grant (up to €3,500) supports research stays of 1–3 weeks, covering travel and accommodation expenses.

Q4: Are the grants open to all disciplines? Yes, both grants are open to all disciplines. However, specific rulings apply to African Studies hosts due to German Research Foundation regulations.

Q5: What are the key selection criteria? Selection is merit-based, focusing on the academic excellence of the applicant and the cooperative project, as evidenced by publications, project design, and potential for networking.

Q6: What support do grantees receive beyond funding? Grantees gain institutional affiliation, access to Bayreuth’s library and research facilities, office and lab space, and integration into the university’s research networks.

Q7: What is expected of grantees during their fellowship? Grantees must collaborate with their local host, utilise Bayreuth’s infrastructure, and submit a report documenting outcomes within 15 months of acceptance.

Q8: Can applicants with families apply? Yes. Starter Grant recipients accompanied by children receive an additional monthly family allowance of €250.

Q9: What is the application process? Applicants must submit a complete application via the online form, including required documents, by September 15, 2026.

Q10: What happens after completing a Starter Grant? Successful grantees may apply for a Booster Grant (€20,000), contingent on documented outcomes such as publications or conferences.

Q11: How does the programme promote diversity? The Centre views diversity as an asset and actively encourages applications from female scholars and individuals who can enhance the university’s research profile.

Q12: What are the reporting requirements? A report must be submitted 15 months after acceptance, documenting project outcomes and contributions.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre Research Grants 2026–2027

Conclusion

The University of Bayreuth Centre of International Excellence “Alexander von Humboldt” Grants 2026–2027 represent a significant opportunity for researchers worldwide to engage in high-quality projects, foster international collaboration, and contribute to Bayreuth’s dynamic academic environment.

The Starter Grant Programme provides substantial funding for ambitious projects, with the potential for follow-up support through the Booster Grant. The Short Term Grant Programme offers targeted support for shorter research stays, enabling scholars to initiate collaborations and explore new directions.

Both programmes emphasise collaboration with local hosts, integration into Bayreuth’s research networks, and adherence to rigorous academic standards. By participating, grantees gain not only financial support but also institutional affiliation, access to resources, and the chance to contribute to a diverse and inclusive research community.

With an application deadline of September 15, 2026, these grants are a gateway to innovation, networking, and scholarly impact. For researchers seeking to expand their horizons and engage with one of Germany’s leading universities, the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre Grants offer a transformative opportunity.

To explore and lean more about other grant opportunities, visit the OFY page HERE.
